subject: Critical Thinking
title: Conditional Probability: When Context Changes Everything
description: A quick, practical guide to Conditional Probability: When Context Changes Everything.

hook.text: The probability of being hit by lightning is 1 in 500,000. But if you're standing in an open field during a storm?

buildup.text: Conditional probability: the likelihood of an event GIVEN that another event has occurred. Context changes the math.

discovery.text: P(A|B): the probability of A given B. It's not the same as P(B|A). Confusing them is a common and dangerous error.

twist.text: The prosecutor's fallacy: P(evidence|innocent) ≠ P(innocent|evidence). Rare evidence doesn't mean rare innocence.

climax.text: Every time someone says 'the odds are X,' ask: 'Given what conditions?' Without context, probabilities are meaningless.

punchline.text: Probability without context is just a number. Context is everything.

details.summary: Conditional probability measures how likely an event is given that another event has already occurred. The probability of rain tomorrow changes dramatically if you know a hurricane is approaching.
details.whyItMatters: Ignoring conditional probability causes errors in medical diagnosis, legal reasoning, and risk assessment whenever context-dependent information is involved.
takeaways: The probability of A given B is often very different from B given A
Confusing these directions is called the prosecutor's fallacy

faq.question: What is the prosecutor's fallacy and why does it matter?
faq.answer: The prosecutor's fallacy confuses the probability of evidence given innocence with the probability of innocence given evidence. A rare DNA match does not mean a suspect is certainly guilty without considering the prior probability.

faq.question: How does conditional probability apply to everyday decisions?
faq.answer: The probability you will enjoy a movie depends on whether you liked the director's previous work. The probability of traffic depends on whether it is a holiday. Every decision improves when you condition on available context.
